scenario: Margaret, a 76-year-old woman who lives alone, taking part in your usual morning wellbeing check-in. Yesterday, Margaret caught her foot on an uneven pavement while walking to the shops. She regained her balance without falling or hitting your head. She has no new pain or dizziness, but the incident frightened her more than she wants to admit. She slept poorly because she kept thinking about what might have happened if nobody had been nearby. This morning, Margaret had tea and toast but decided to skip her usual walk. She normally meet her friend Jean at a café on Mondays and look forward to it. She has not cancelled yet, although she is considering telling Jean that she is too busy. Margaret's daughter lives nearby, but she hesitate to call because she is working, and Margaret do not want her to think that she can no longer manage on her own.
